# Switch NX2 - read when the Veshiru GUI starts.
# One NAME=VALUE per line. Lines starting with # are ignored.
# A variable already set in the environment wins over this file.
# Between files, the user copy (%APPDATA%\veshiru\nx2_switches.txt, or
# $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/veshiru/nx2_switches.txt) wins over this one. A portable install also reads
# user/nx2_switches.txt next to its data, and that copy wins last. Editing this file is never
# needed: copy the lines you want into your own and restart.
# Beside-application files accept EDEN_NX2_* and the emulator's diagnostic switches only.
# Host environment settings, including library paths such as EDEN_STREAMLINE_DIR, must be
# set in the real environment or the user configuration file at an absolute config location.
#
# Restart the emulator after editing.

# --- Performance tuning defaults for Switch 2 ---
# Offload GPU method/macro execution to the back thread (SPLIT=2 delivers up to +54% FPS alone).
EDEN_NX2_SPLIT=2

# Batch GPU fence syncpoints to reduce host driver overhead and smooth frametimes.
EDEN_NX2_FENCE_BATCH=1

# Keep more decompressed NUP members in host RAM. The Veshiru target machine has 32 GB, so 1 GiB
# avoids re-decoding area changes without pressuring the GTX 1650's 4 GB of VRAM. Minimum 64 MiB.
EDEN_NX2_NUP_CACHE_MIB=1024

# Texture-cache collector overrides. The GUI setting texture_cache_memory_limit is the primary
# control (0 = Auto = three quarters of the GPU budget). These can raise thresholds for testing,
# but never past the live driver budget. EDEN_NX2_TC_LOG=1 logs threshold changes.
#EDEN_NX2_TC_EXPECTED_MIB=2048
#EDEN_NX2_TC_CRITICAL_MIB=3072
#EDEN_NX2_TC_LOG=1

# Serve a sound sibling for a damaged .zs NUP member so a bad dump can still boot. Set 0 to expose
# the damaged member instead (strict compatibility testing).
#EDEN_NUP_DAMAGED_FALLBACK=0

# Leave buffer downloads disabled on Switch 2 (default): forcing downloads (=1) copies back
# 90-220 MB/s of buffers CPU never touches, causing heavy mutex contention and dropping FPS by ~38-63%.
#EDEN_NX2_BUFFER_DOWNLOADS=1

# Which fence the game waits for when it presents. 1 = the previous frame's: the game prepares the
# next frame while the GPU finishes this one, and waits for this one too while the GPU is behind.
# 0 = this frame's: no overlap. Any value other than 1 means 0, so =2 does not run two frames ahead.
# Unset: per title. Ocarina of Time uses 1, Donkey Kong Bananza 0, and other titles wait for this
# frame unless a GPU channel waits on a semaphore the game releases after the present.
# Ocarina of Time with =0 (or =2): 30.9 fps against 38.9 unset, same spot and settings.
#EDEN_NX2_FRAMES_AHEAD=1

# --- Workarounds / Debug ---
# Terrain/indirect drawing fix for Donkey Kong Bananza: enabled by default. Set to 0 only to leave to GPU.
#EDEN_NX2_RESETFIX=0

# Drop reactive-flushing read traps on Switch 2 programs (opt-in; can reduce FPS from 29 to 24 in MKW).
#EDEN_NX2_NO_REACTIVE=1

#EDEN_NX2_MME_JIT=0
#EDEN_NX2_PBFLUSH=0
#EDEN_NX2_SKIP_SAME=0
#EDEN_NX2_INLINE_DEFER=0
#EDEN_NX2_SPLIT_SKIP=1
#EDEN_NX2_AUTO_STUB=1
#EDEN_NX2_KEEP_ASTC=1
# Size the temporary ASTC decode images exactly (=0) instead of rounding them up to a multiple of 64
# texels so textures of nearly the same size share one.
#EDEN_NX2_ASTC_SCRATCH_BUCKET=0
# Submit after the ASTC decode (=0) instead of recording the decode and the BC encode in one submit.
#EDEN_NX2_ASTC_ONE_SUBMIT=0
# Only move finished ASTC decode images back to the pool once a frame, and drop the newest one when
# the pool is full (=0), instead of when a texture asks for one and evicting the oldest.
#EDEN_NX2_ASTC_POOL_V2=0
# Only reuse an ASTC decode image of exactly the size asked for (=0), not a larger one.
#EDEN_NX2_ASTC_POOL_FIT=0
